clue.text: Very big to Macron is abnormal

indicators.note: something abnormal is out of its usual shape, so the preceding letters must be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; it doubles as part of the signal

explanation.surface: A comment that the French president finds something unusually enormous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' does double duty: its letters join the mix and it also reads as part of 'is abnormal'.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomic describes figures as vast as distances between stars, hence enormous or huge.

clue.text: Press coverage of nurse held by TV writer

indicators.note: providing coverage of something means wrapping round it, so the press word encloses the nurse
what is held by something sits inside it, so these pieces go within the two letters

blocks.note: taken as written; it splits around the rest
to press someone is to urge them
EN is an Enrolled Nurse

explanation.surface: A television dramatist gets newspaper coverage of a nurse story.
explanation.walkthrough: Ivan Turgenev was a Russian novelist and dramatist, author of Fathers and Sons; 'TV writer' looks like a single phrase but TV is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan Turgenev was a nineteenth-century Russian novelist and playwright, so an example of the category named.

clue.text: Insult can disconcert

blocks.note: to dis someone is slang for insulting them
'may' and 'can' both express permission or possibility

explanation.surface: A warning that a rude remark is capable of upsetting someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismay someone is to unsettle or alarm them, a close synonym for throwing them off balance.

clue.text: Encouragement for thug

blocks.note: first meaning: '...!', a spoken urging to continue
second meaning: a hired heavy or ruffian

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses differ only in the space: 'go on' as a cheer, and the single word for a hired tough.
explanation.definitionFit: A goon is slang for a hired heavy or bully, while the spaced phrase is a cheering shout urging someone forward.

clue.text: ‘Art’ models entertaining Troy by doing stuff – looking good!

indicators.note: to model clay is to reshape it, so the quoted word's letters get reformed
a host entertaining a guest has them inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
t is the abbreviation for troy weight
someone doing stuff is busy and lively

explanation.surface: Life models in an art class host a man named Troy and keep busy, all looking splendid.
explanation.walkthrough: Troy looks like a name, but troy weight is the system used for weighing precious metals, abbreviated t.
explanation.definitionFit: Attractive means pleasing to the eye, which is what someone or something good-looking is.

clue.text: Copper? One should be quicker

blocks.note: first meaning, cryptic: 'cop' is the clipped, abbreviated version of the word copper
second meaning: a faster route than the usual one

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful sense: 'cop' is copper trimmed down, so it is literally a shortened form of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A short cut is a quicker route, and copper clipped to 'cop' is the same phrase read as a truncated word.

clue.text: My working day involved getting bird

indicators.note: something involved is wrapped up within something else, so these pieces go inside the exclamation

blocks.note: 'Cor!' is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'My!'
a machine that is on is working
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: Someone's working day included a bird sighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' looks possessive, but it is an exclamation of surprise; the inserted pieces go just after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The condor is a huge South American vulture, one of the largest flying birds in the world.

clue.text: One’s foolish accepting current contractual disclaimer

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so a letter goes inside

blocks.note: one who is foolish is an ass
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Someone is a fool for signing a deal with a get-out clause about electricity.
explanation.walkthrough: I for current is the physics symbol used in electrical formulas.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods sold 'as is' come with no guarantee about their condition, a standard phrase waiving the seller's liability.

clue.text: After drink I turn into child and fight

indicators.note: one thing going into another ends up inside it

blocks.note: a slug is a gulp of strong drink
taken as written
a tot is a small child
a U-turn, so U stands for a turn

explanation.surface: After a drink, someone transforms into a child and starts a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' simply places the drink first; 'turn' stands for the U of a U-turn.
explanation.definitionFit: To slug it out is to fight hard to the finish, an idiom for a bruising contest.

clue.text: Gives warning of streak when cycling

indicators.note: cycling moves letters round in a loop, so the front letter goes to the back

blocks.note: to streak past is to shoot past

explanation.surface: A cyclist sounds a warning to someone streaking by.
explanation.walkthrough: The S at the front of SHOOT moves to the end. 'Cycling' suggests bicycles, but it signals the letter rotation.
explanation.definitionFit: A driver who hoots sounds the horn to warn others, so the verb means alerting people.

clue.text: Soldiers missing out end of assault course

indicators.note: missing something out means leaving it off, so a letter is dropped
the end of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: a regiment is a body of soldiers
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Troops skip the last part of their assault course training.
explanation.walkthrough: REGIMENT loses its T. 'Assault course' looks like a single phrase, but 'course' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A regimen is a prescribed course of diet, exercise or treatment followed over time.

clue.text: Functions originally twice on screen

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so the doubled piece is placed first

blocks.note: RE means on or concerning, taken two times
dos are parties or social functions

explanation.surface: An instruction about software functions showing up twice on a monitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screen' suggests a computer, but a REREDOS is an ornamental screen behind a church altar.
explanation.definitionFit: A reredos is a decorated partition or panel standing behind an altar, a church furnishing that acts as a backdrop.

clue.text: Au pair maybe a horny type

blocks.note: first meaning: a carer employed to look after children
second meaning: a female goat, which has horns

explanation.walkthrough: 'Horny' suggests lust, but it means having horns: the nanny goat.
explanation.definitionFit: An au pair is one kind of live-in childminder, and a she-goat is called by the same word.

clue.text: F1 drivers at first suitably placed (they’ll be in the pack)

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word before
placed suitably means put in a fitting spot, here within the vehicles

blocks.note: taken as written
an ace counts as one in cards
the machines that do the driving in Formula One
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Formula One drivers take sensible positions on the grid, with a hint about the pack of racers.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'pack' in the brackets is a pack of playing cards, not the racing field; 'suitably' hints at suits.
explanation.definitionFit: Kings, queens and jacks are court cards found in every deck, so they're part of the pack.

clue.text: A good way to describe extraordinary actions which can go to one’s head

definitions.text: which can go to one’s head

indicators.note: something extraordinary is out of the ordinary order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a good way off is far
taken as written

explanation.surface: A recommendation for describing remarkable deeds that might make someone conceited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go to one's head' suggests vanity; read literally, it is something worn on the head. A FASCINATOR is a small decorative headpiece worn at weddings and races.
explanation.definitionFit: A fascinator is an ornamental headpiece of feathers or flowers, so it literally sits on the wearer's head.

clue.text: Growing old disgracefully – seen taking cocaine in tantrum

indicators.note: behaving disgracefully means not in proper order, so these letters are rearranged
one thing in another sits inside it

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
to make a scene is to throw a tantrum
C is slang shorthand for cocaine

explanation.surface: Ageing badly: a person spotted using drugs mid-meltdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Growing old disgracefully' reads as one phrase, but 'disgracefully' belongs to the wordplay; the drug goes in before the tantrum's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Senescence is the biological process of ageing and deterioration with time.

clue.text: Vomits now flying in turbulence – let’s change the subject

indicators.note: turbulence is violent disorder, so these letters are thrown about

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A passenger is sick on a bumpy flight and others would rather talk about something else.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a conversational way of steering away from an awkward topic to the next matter.

clue.text: Had forgotten an arrangement? Never going to happen

indicators.note: an arrangement puts things into a new order, so the preceding letters are reorganised

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a plan slipped another person's mind and is told it never would.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an emphatic reply dismissing any possibility, much like saying something will not occur.

clue.text: Youngster carrying gun? Great place for a holiday!

indicators.note: someone carrying something holds it, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: a youth is a young person
an arm is a weapon such as a gun

explanation.surface: An armed teenager prompts an ironic cheer about a wonderful resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great' is not praise: Great Yarmouth is a seaside resort in Norfolk, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Great Yarmouth is a traditional English seaside holiday town, so the opening adjective belongs to its full name.

clue.text: Flashy female writer in church, a happy place

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

blocks.note: CE is the Church of England
loud clothes are showy
Anaïs Nin was a French-American diarist and novelist

explanation.surface: A showy woman author in church finds contentment.
explanation.walkthrough: Anaïs Nin is the female writer; the church abbreviation splits around the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on cloud nine is an idiom for blissful elation, so it names a state of great happiness.

clue.text: I’ll briefly show up as a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter is dropped
up as in stirred up or mixed up, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the contraction's letters, ignoring the apostrophe
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone promises to appear briefly in the role of an MP.
explanation.walkthrough: A parliament is the collective noun for a group of owls, so a member of one behaves in an owl-like way.
explanation.definitionFit: A parliament of owls is the group name, so a member of that gathering would be like an owl.

clue.text: Root of word Irish in essence

indicators.note: the essence of something is its core, so only the central letters are kept

blocks.note: the two central letters
the three central letters

explanation.surface: An etymology question: the origin of a word in Irish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Root of word' suggests etymology, but 'Root' alone is the definition: orris root comes from iris plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Orris is the fragrant dried rootstock of certain irises, used in perfumes and gin.

clue.text: See 17
Dish in Battle of Lepanto?

indicators.note: a battle is a chaotic melee, so the letters that follow are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A question whether some meal was served at the 1571 naval Battle of Lepanto.
explanation.definitionFit: Polenta is an Italian dish of boiled cornmeal, fitting since Lepanto involved Venetian forces.

clue.text: Pledge from father son ignored

indicators.note: what is ignored is left out, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: to father offspring is to spawn them
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A promise made by a dad that his boy disregards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father' looks like a noun, but it is the verb meaning to produce young; SPAWN loses its S.
explanation.definitionFit: To pawn something is to deposit it as security for a loan, so it is a pledge.

clue.text: Success in following had the desired effect

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the second piece is placed behind the first

blocks.note: a hit is a success
someone who is in is at home

explanation.surface: Achievement in pursuing a goal worked as intended.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark that hits home strikes its target and makes its intended impact on the listener.

clue.text: Off on 19

blocks.note: first meaning: gone bad, like meat that smells
second meaning: elated, being on the answer to 19 across

explanation.walkthrough: 19 across is CLOUD NINE; someone on cloud nine is euphoric. 'Off' and 'on' look like opposites, but both lead to the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: Game meat that has gone off is described as high, and someone blissfully elated is also high.

clue.text: Refuse answer to question, ‘Which Lawrence joined the RAF?’

blocks.note: the reply is framed 'it was ...'
T.E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia, enlisted in the RAF under an assumed name

explanation.surface: Declining to answer a quiz question about a famous Lawrence.
explanation.walkthrough: The reply to the question is 'it was T.E.'. 'Refuse' looks like a verb but is the noun for rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Refuse is household rubbish, discarded material that people throw away.

clue.text: Frenzied royal companion caught at last drinking wine

indicators.note: the letter for caught goes to the end, so the front letter moves round to the back
drinking takes something inside, so one piece is held within the other

blocks.note: the Queen's corgis were famous royal pets
Asti is an Italian sparkling wine

explanation.surface: A wild companion of a royal gets caught boozing.
explanation.walkthrough: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught; CORGI's C moves to the end to give ORGIC, then ASTI goes in before the C.
explanation.definitionFit: Orgiastic describes wild, unrestrained revelry, so frenzied and abandoned in behaviour.
